system.name: PARTONOMY
system.one_liner: Benchmark for pixel-level part grounding in large multimodal models via Explanatory Part Segmentation, plus PLUM, a segmenting LMM using span tagging and feedback.

content.variant_note: five tinted task cards of photo plus chat-style question and answer, a question-answer mutation card, and a strip of part-mask thumbnails
content.argues: PARTONOMY asks LMMs five kinds of part questions (identification, intersection, difference, part-to-whole, whole-to-part) and requires answers justified by part masks; question-answer mutation builds hard answer choices.
content.subject: Five task cards of user questions and PLUM answers on photos, a question-answer mutation card, and a strip of part-mask thumbnails.

encoding.color_means: card tint groups the five task cards into three families (peach, blue, green; family names not written); olive-grey bubble = user question, mauve bubble = PLUM answer; cyan paint on photos = a part mask; peach pill = mutation operation

encoding.marker_means: Q: and A: label question and answer; plus, circular arrows and minus name add, replace and remove (inferred from how the answers differ)
encoding.emphasis: bold italic part words in every bubble and the painted masks on the photos; PLUM (Ours) in the legend marks the proposed model
reusable_patterns: tinted task cards where the tint says which task family a card belongs to

key words in bold italic in the answer, mirrored by painted masks on the photo

lessons.what_to_learn: Show a benchmark's task families as small tinted chat cards, one real question and answer on a photo per card, with the key words in bold italic and the matching mask painted on the picture; group cards by tint and give data construction one extra card beside them.
lessons.suits: Benchmark or task papers for multimodal models where several task types can each be shown with one real question, answer and visual evidence.

evidence: The PARTONOMY dataset evaluates LMMs’ part understanding through the Explanatory Part Segmentation task.
Our question-answer mutation framework generates challenging answer choices by predicting part co-occurrence and by selecting parts from confusable objects.

summary: PARTONOMY is a benchmark for pixel-level part grounding in large multimodal models, built around the Explanatory Part Segmentation task, and PLUM is the paper's segmenting model that uses span tagging and a feedback loop. Figure 1 is a dense gallery of six tinted cards on a white ground. Five task cards (Part Identification, Part Intersection, Part Difference, Part-to-Whole, Whole-to-Part) each show a photo, the user's question and PLUM's answer as chat bubbles with avatars, with part words in bold italic and painted masks on the photos. A sixth card shows question-answer mutation: an answer is changed by add, replace and remove operations into three alternative answer choices. A strip of ten photos names and masks parts of an airplane and a torpedo.
summary_zh: PARTONOMY 是评测大模型部件级分割的基准。图 1 由六张彩色卡片组成：五张任务卡（识别、交集、差异、部件到整体、整体到部件）以聊天气泡展示提问、回答和部件蒙版，一张展示问答变异生成干扰选项，底部是十张部件照片条。
notes: The pre-screen put contribution-mosaic first; scope-overview is used instead because every card is a task example, not a separate contribution. The role of the bottom strip (painted part masks, repeating the airplane and torpedo parts) and the meaning of the three operation pills are read from the drawing and the caption, not stated in the paper text. The three tints probably match the three question classes mentioned in the paper but the classes are not named in the figure.
